| [CORE-0002](core/CORE-0002-budget-governs-clock-speed.md) | accepted | — | Budget is the independent variable and clock speed is derived from it | Model spend has a hard ceiling per real day, and the simulation's clock speed is whatever that ceiling affords; the unit of cost is the decision point, not the tick. |
| [CORE-0003](core/CORE-0003-simulated-clock.md) | accepted | — | Run on a simulated clock advanced by a discrete-event scheduler | Sim time is an integer count of sim-seconds from a seeded epoch, advanced only inside the tick transaction, with a 15-sim-minute scheduler quantum and pacing set by the budget governor. |
| [CORE-0004](core/CORE-0004-backpressure-slows-the-clock.md) | accepted | `py/src/jeve/llm/**` | Slow the clock under backpressure; never default a decision | The tick is a barrier: sim time does not advance until every decision due at that tick has a real answer, so a slow model means a slow world and a dead model means a paused world. |
| [CORE-0005](core/CORE-0005-path-derived-randomness.md) | accepted | — | Replay from the recorded log, and derive every random draw from a path | A recorded run replays to a byte-identical event log from its stored model responses, never by re-querying; every random draw is a pure function of a path (`seed, agent, decision_seq, question`), so no RNG state exists to persist. |

| [CORE-0007](core/CORE-0007-postgres-one-transaction-per-tick.md) | accepted | — | Persist to Postgres with one transaction per tick and a causal event log | Every tick commits its domain mutations, events, decisions, scheduler changes and clock advance in a single transaction; events are append-only and carry a `causes` array of the event ids that led to them. |
| [DECIDE-0001](../py/src/jeve/decide/decisions/DECIDE-0001-one-request-per-decision-point.md) | accepted | — | Send one request per decision point carrying the whole decision surface | An agent is evaluated only at a decision point — task complete, inbox item over an importance floor, schedule boundary, synchronous interaction, or a mandatory timer — and that one request carries every question the role might need. |
| [DECIDE-0002](../py/src/jeve/decide/decisions/DECIDE-0002-two-tier-escalation.md) | accepted | — | Escalate on confidence in two tiers, and keep the first tier typed | Tier 1 re-asks only the uncertain questions of a flash LLM through TypeSafe's adapter, which returns the same typed response shape; tier 2 is generative and fires only on an ontology gap or when a viewer needs prose. |
